title: Preparation and Characterization of Alginate‐Based Bioinks for 3D Bioprinting of Cell‐Laden Constructs
author: Dahlan, Ketabat, et al.
materials: For 500 ml:435 ml cell culture medium (Gibco Advanced DMEM/F12, 1×, reduced serum medium; Fisher Scientific, cat no. 12634010); store at 4°C50 ml fetal bovine serum (FBS), heat inactivated (10% v/v final) (Fischer Scientific, cat. no. A5256801)5 ml anti‐anti (1% v/v final, Gibco antibiotic‐antimycotic, 100×; Fisher Scientific, cat no. 15240062); store at –20°C; aliquot the reagent into working volumes and avoid freeze/thaw cycles10 ml HAT supplement (2% v/v final, Gibco HAT supplement, 50×; Fisher Scientific, cat no. 21060017); store at –20°C; aliquot the reagent into working volumes and avoid freeze/thaw cyclesStore up to 6 months at 4°C

steps.title: Label culture flasks
steps.instruction: Write cell name, passage number, date, and your initials on each culture flask before use.

steps.title: Sterilize materials and set up BSC
steps.instruction: Wipe culture flasks, serological pipettes, and pipette pump with 70 % ethanol, allow to air‑dry, then place all items inside a biological safety cabinet (BSC).

steps.title: Prepare HUVEC complete medium (500 mL)
steps.instruction: In a sterile container combine 435 mL Gibco Advanced DMEM/F12 (1× reduced serum), 50 mL heat‑inactivated fetal bovine serum (10 % v/v final, Fisher cat A5256801), 5 mL antibiotic‑antimycotic (1 % v/v final, Gibco 100×, Fisher cat 15240062), and 10 mL HAT supplement (2 % v/v final, Gibco 50×, Fisher cat 21060017) to total 500 mL. Store the complete medium at 4 °C for up to 6 months; keep the FBS, anti‑anti, and HAT aliquots at –20 °C and avoid freeze‑thaw cycles.

steps.title: Thaw and expand HUVECs
steps.instruction: Begin thawing frozen HUVECs at least 1 week before planned bioprinting; seed cells in the prepared complete medium and maintain them under standard culture conditions until they reach the desired density for bioink preparation.

steps.title: Prepare 0.1 % PEI coating solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve polyethyleneimine (PEI) in sterile water to a final concentration of 0.1 % (w/v); filter‑sterilize if needed. Prepare this solution one day before bioprinting.

steps.title: Coat culture plates with PEI
steps.instruction: Add enough 0.1 % PEI solution to cover each culture plate, incubate for the recommended time, then aspirate excess and rinse gently with sterile water before use.

steps.title: Prepare concentrated hydrogel mix (Day 1)
steps.instruction: Calculate a 70 % higher polymer concentration than the target: for a final 3 % (w/v) alginate and 1 % (w/v) gelatin, dissolve 4.28 % (w/v) alginate and 1.43 % (w/v) gelatin in sterile water to make the hydrogel mix. Mix thoroughly until fully dissolved.

steps.title: Store hydrogel mix at 4 °C
steps.instruction: Keep the prepared hydrogel mix at 4 °C; it may be stored for 1–2 days but prolonged storage is not recommended.

steps.title: Warm culture medium to room temperature
steps.instruction: Allow the complete culture medium to reach room temperature naturally; do not place it in a water bath to avoid degradation of components.

steps.title: Mix hydrogel with cell suspension (70:30)
steps.instruction: Harvest HUVECs, resuspend them in the warmed complete medium, then combine the hydrogel mix with the cell suspension in a 70 % hydrogel : 30 % cell‑medium volume ratio. This yields a final bioink containing approximately 3 % alginate and 1 % gelatin.

steps.title: Bioprint cell‑laden constructs
steps.instruction: Load the freshly prepared cell‑laden bioink into the bioprinter and print within 1 hour of mixing; complete the printing session within 3–4 hours to limit shear‑induced cellular stress.

steps.title: Stain constructs for viability
steps.instruction: Add 0.5 mL of viability staining solution to each well containing constructs or scaffolds less than 1 mm in height, ensuring full coverage; incubate according to the staining protocol.

steps.title: Perform rheology analysis
steps.instruction: Run rheological measurements on the bioink samples; each run typically requires 1–3 hours depending on the number of samples.

steps.title: Conduct immunofluorescence staining
steps.instruction: Fix printed constructs, then incubate sequentially with primary and secondary antibodies; allocate up to 2 days total for the immunofluorescence assay.
